newsitem.title: UK: Conservative EU muddle damaging Britain-UK's Blair.
newsitem.headline: Conservative EU muddle damaging Britain-UK's Blair.

text.p: Labour leader Tony Blair said on Thursday that Conservative Eurosceptics will stand at the coming election on an entirely separate manifesto from that officially espoused by Prime Minister John Major.

Responding to news that Conservative headquarters had promised not to censor the election addresses of candidates who wished to declare their outright opposition to a single European currency, Blair said confusion would result.

"It is very clear that you have now got, what, 100 or 150 Conservative candidates standing effectively on an entirely different manifesto from the Conservative leadership," he told a London conference of students studying politics.
"The country does not know where it is, the rest of Europe does not know where it is with Britain, and that damages Britain's interests," he added.

Sir Marcus Fox, chairman of the committee that represents rank-and-file Conservative MPs, said on Wednesday he had been assured by party chairman Brian Mawhinney there would be no editing of personal messages on Conservative candidates' election addresses.
Blair admitted that the Labour line on the single currency was similar to Major's -- a wait-and-see policy.
"We don't know what is going to happen over the next few years, and it would be foolish for us to close off the option altogether now and say we are never going to do it," he said.
But Blair said it was essential that Britain remain in the European Union and it was worrying that the Conservatives were drifting ever closer towards suggesting a pull-out.
"If we end up withdrawing from the EU, we will harm jobs, we will harm industry and we will harm immeasurably Britain's influence and standing in the world," he said.
"What I feel when I look at the present-day Conservative Party is that it is lurching more and more to that position."
